newsitem.title: ITALY: Bell Atlantic snatches Omnitel stake.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic snatches Omnitel stake.

text.p: U.S. telecoms group Bell Atlantic on Monday snatched a deal to increase its stake in Italy's mobile phone group Omnitel and so scupper at the last moment German group's Mannesmann's hopes of purchase.

Omnitel's largest shareholder Olivetti announced in a statement that Bell had exercised its pre-emptive rights to buy the 8.26 percent stake in Omnitel Sistemi Radiocellulari (OSR) that Mannesmann believed it had clinched last month.

The loss-making Olivetti had put the OSR stake up for sale to help cut its hefty debts and restructure its trouble portfolio of computer and telecoms businesses. Olivetti is the major shareholder in OSR, which in turn owns 70 percent of Italy's second mobile phone operator Omnitel.

An Olivetti spokesman confirmed the deal had been completed and Bell would buy the 8.26 percent stake in OSR -- or a 5.8 percent indirect stake in Omnitel -- on the same terms as Mannesmann agreed, that is to pay 432.5 billion lire ($283 million).

Last month, Mannesmann which was already a shareholder in Omnitel signed a contract to buy the 8.26 percent stake from Olivetti, but as required by the by-laws of OSR, the sale was subject to pre-emptive rights of the other shareholders.

These shareholders which included Swedish state-owned telecoms operator Telia, U.S. Cellular Communications International Inc (CCIL), as well as Bell and Olivetti, had thirty days to exercise their rights on the same terms as stipulated in the Mannesmann contract which was to be activated in early to mid November.

Olivetti confirmed that Bell, which already had a 16.9 percent stake in OSR, was exercising its right to buy the stake bringing its total up to 24.9 percent, while other OSR partners CCIL and Telia had not exercised their rights.

The deal is a clear blow to Mannesmann who believed it had snatched a deal to expand its telecoms interest outside Germany, while Olivetti were keen to stress the deal showed the attractiveness of Omnitel to overseas investors.
Olivetti had only bought the 8.26 percent stake from Lehman Brothers in late 1995 for 283 billion lire and then had to add a further 45 billion lire as an equity injection.

Olivetti's Omnitel stake is considered as one the ailing group's most valuable assets as it struggles to sell off its loss-making personal computer businesses, reduced debts and finance its expansion into the telecoms area.
Omnitel launched its mobile phone service in December 1995 and quickly attracted over 500,000 subscribers in competition with the state-controlled Telecom Italia Mobile TIM.

With the deal now complete, OSR shareholders consist of Olivetti with 50.7 percent, Bell 24.9 percent, CCIL 14.7 percent and Telia at 9.7 percent. Shareholders in Pronto Italia, which owns the other 30 percent of Omnitel, include U.S. group Airtouch with 51.5 percent and Mannesmann 19.8 percent with other group with 28.7 percent.

Overall indirect stake in Omnitel include Olivetti with 35.5 percent, Bell 17.4 percent, Airtouch 15.5 percent, CCIL 10.3 percent, Telia 6.8 percent, Mannesmann 5.9 percent, and others at 8.6 percent. ($1=1,526 lire)
